A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FATE benchmark study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, prompt ablations, expert questionnaire results, and analyses of generated proofs.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds model comparisons, a human problem-solving study, and computational-budget analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, whole-proof generation, prompts, and verification procedure remain substantively unchanged. The new retrieval-augmented generation suggestion in Section 4.4 is a proposed research direction, not an implemented component.

E1.justification: The algebra domains and FATE-M/H/X collections remain unchanged at 150/100/100 problems. Section 3.2 adds a human-solving evaluation involving algebra PhD students and postdoctoral researchers, extending the evaluated population beyond the existing model evaluations and professor questionnaire.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 9 add Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking. Table 2 adds Goedel-Prover-V2 and Kimina-Prover to the natural-language comparison, which previously contained only DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-Prover-V2. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include randomly assigning each human participant five non-overlapping problems with a 2.5-hour limit, and selecting model-specific sampling budgets using model size times average output tokens times sample count (Section F.1.4). The original pass@64, 64k-token evaluation remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The human study adds direct evidence about the H-to-X difficulty progression. Section F.1.4 adds an analysis of model performance under approximately normalized computational budgets. Existing prompt ablations, error analyses, and reasoning case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 64 samples per problem and the same unbiased pass@k estimator in Section F.1.3. v3 adds no seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Its model-specific k values concern inference budgets rather than a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Matched existing results are unchanged. Additions include Qwen3's 16%/0%/0% formal accuracy on M/H/X; Goedel and Kimina natural-language accuracies of 48%/8% and 35%/3% on H/X; and human accuracies of 73%/21%. Section 3.2 newly reports that 38% of FATE-X problems require new definitions, averaging 2.4 each. Table 10 adds results under the new normalized-budget protocol, rather than same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical content of the benchmark examples, illustrative arguments, and pass@k estimator is unchanged. The added computational-cost proxy is an evaluation control, without a new theorem, proof, or substantive revision to formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, difficulty progression, 3%/0% best formal accuracies on H/X, formalization bottleneck, and reflection findings. Additional evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly suggests retrieving Mathlib theorems and accurate type information to address common formalization errors. Section 4.3.3 extends its comparison to the expanded set of specialized provers. The principal bottleneck interpretation and existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section F.1.2 newly specifies Mathlib 4.13.0, 4.16.0, and 4.19.0 for M/H/X, a 300-second timeout, and a preloaded Mathlib cache. These are newly disclosed settings, with no evidence that they changed from v1. Table 10 also supplies model sizes, output lengths, and allocated sampling budgets.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Qwen3 technical report by Yang et al. (2025) alongside its evaluation. The broader related-work discussion and positioning against contest and university mathematics benchmarks remain unchanged; consolidating the duplicate Lean 4 reference does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: v3 lightly edits the curation narrative, revises the difficulty-evidence paragraph, updates acknowledgments and publication metadata, and adds Section F.1.4. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact; the earlier model-based difficulty statistics remain in Appendix B.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-part Table 10, expands Tables 1, 2, and 9, and reorders Table 2. Typography, code rendering, conference headers, and page flow change, while Figures 1–4 retain their content and the overall single-column presentation is preserved.

improvement.justification: v3 provides broader evidence for the natural-language/formalization gap, adds human difficulty validation and a computational-budget comparison, and makes verification more reproducible through explicit Mathlib versions and timeout settings. These are useful extensions to v1's existing evidence. The human study still omits its participant count, and budget normalization uses an approximate cost proxy, limiting the strength of the added support.
